title: The Air Merchant's Atonement
logline: An aging merchant who once endowed a free life-support reserve for destitute miners must undo his own charitable trust after a tenement boss exploits the free air to run a deadly sweatshop.

roles.description: An aging environmental equipment dealer; weary, respected, appalled that his youth's philanthropy became an engine of abuse.
Tenement administrator running an illegal high-heat smelter in the living quarters; smug, ruthless, claiming an unalterable lease.
An armed security cutter patrolling the tenement perimeter to protect the illegal foundry operations.
An aggressive salvage and smelting syndicate extracting metal in residential sectors to avoid municipal fees.
A crowded orbital tenement block where hundreds of miners sleep beside sweltering unventilated workshops.
An industrial parts depot stocking certified municipal metering valves and pressure restrictors.

public_situation: An aging oxygen dealer tries to install commercial restrictor valves on a free life-support manifold in {role:tenement_habitat}, prompting protests from the landlord.
private_truth: {role:block_overseer} is using {role:air_merchant}'s thirty-year-old charitable air charter to run an unregistered smelting furnace inside the residential barracks.

beats.public_change: Notice boards at {role:foundry_depot} log a rush requisition for heavy industrial flow-limiting restrictor valves.

missions.reason: He hires an independent pilot to purchase certified flow restrictor valves at the depot and deliver them to the habitat maintenance hatch.
missions.private_fact: He endowed the free life-support trust thirty years ago to protect destitute miners, never imagining it would fuel a landlord's sweatshop.

beats.public_change: Temperatures climb throughout {role:tenement_habitat} as toxic exhaust filters back into residential ventilation shafts.

missions.reason: He asks the pilot to scan the habitat's heat exhaust vents to prove the charitable air allowance is feeding an illegal smelting forge.
missions.private_fact: The landlord pays nothing for life support and threatens to sue him for breach of contract if he cuts the flow.

beats.public_change: An armed syndicate vessel takes up an intercept vector near the habitat docking bay to block technicians from fitting the restrictors.

missions.reason: The merchant needs the armed cutter neutralized so technicians can reach the intake manifold with the restrictor hardware.
missions.private_fact: The cutter captain hails mid-fight offering a share of the foundry's illicit profits if the pilot smashes the restrictors.

player_choice.prompt: With the security cutter disabled and the proof documented, the pilot holds the deed revocation code and the hardware to decide the habitat's fate.

options.label: Revoke the endowment and install meters, shutting down the foundry but forcing miners to pay for air
Transfer the air charter directly to an independent miners' council, cutting out both landlord and merchant
Leave the manifold untouched to preserve the free air for residents despite the sweltering foundry

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot installs the restrictors and executes the revocation of the merchant's original charitable endowment.
resolutions.summary: {role:air_merchant} revokes his trust and meters the intake. The illegal smelter collapses, but impoverished miners must now pay for their breath.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot helped an old merchant dismantle his own charitable air trust to break up an illegal foundry.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot delivers the deed and codes to the resident miners' mutual aid committee.
resolutions.summary: Tenement drillers seize control of the intake manifold. {role:block_overseer} is expelled, while {role:air_merchant} loses all legal claim to his equipment.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot turned an old merchant's air trust over to tenement workers, who barricaded their own life support.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot accepts the enforcer's bribe or walks away without installing the restrictors.
resolutions.summary: The challenge collapses. {role:block_overseer} expands the unmetered foundry, choking {role:tenement_habitat} with fumes while {role:air_merchant} flees in shame.

loose_threads.detail: A handwritten codicil on the air trust deed bears an unfamiliar clerk seal stamped six months before the merchant retired.
Thermal exhaust plumes from the habitat manifold show heavy smelting flux residues registered to a shell company in another sector.
Station commodity boards show a single brokerage bought up all industrial cylinder buybacks hours before the metering dispute began.

radio_hooks: Tenement residents complain of suffocating heat as unmetered foundry lines run overnight.
Municipal council reviews historic philanthropic air covenants dating back thirty cycles.
Hardware suppliers report sudden shortage of commercial life-support flow limiters.

voice_direction.air_merchant: Weary, precise, and burdened with remorse. Speaks in measured, formal sentences and avoids using colloquial slang or commercial jargon.
voice_direction.block_overseer: Brisk, entitled, and aggressive. Speaks rapidly with transactional certainty and repeatedly quotes contractual clauses to shut down objections.
